Match List–I with List–II and select the correct answer using the codes given below.
List–I (Libraries) List–II (Established in and at)

a. Vignana Chandrika Grandhamandali
I. Kovvur, 1916

b. Srikrishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam
II. Hyderabad, 1906

c. Andhra Council of Research
III. Hyderabad, 1901

d. Andhra Saraswati Parishad
IV. Hyderabad, 1922
x:
The Srikrishnadevaraya Andhra Bhasha Nilayam, established in Hyderabad in 1901, was one of the earliest Telugu libraries in the Hyderabad State. It played a crucial role in promoting Telugu language and literature. The Vignana Chandrika Grandhamandali was founded in Hyderabad in 1906 to publish books and encourage intellectual activity among Telugu-speaking people. The Andhra Council of Research was established at Kovvur in 1916 with the objective of encouraging historical and literary research relating to Andhra. The Andhra Saraswati Parishad, founded in Hyderabad in 1922, became an important institution for promoting Telugu language, literature and education. Thus, the correct matching is a–II, b–III, c–I, d– IV, corresponding to Option (3).
Exam Note: Prominent libraries and literary bodies established across Coastal Andhra and Rayalaseema:
• Saraswathi Mahal Library (Thanjavur, 1700s): While located in Tamil Nadu, it holds one of the most vital historical collections of ancient Telugu palm-leaf manuscripts preserved by the Raghunatha Nayaka kings.
• Gautami Regional Library / Gautami Grandhalayam (Rajahmundry, 1898): Formed by merging the Vasuraya Grandhalayam and the Town Hall Library. It is one of the oldest public libraries in the state.
• The Reading Club (Kolluru, Guntur, 1899): One of the earliest rural library initiatives in the Guntur district.
• Youngmen's Literary Association (Guntur, 1900): Created to foster intellectual dialogue and provide access to newspaper
